intro_band.agent_remit_summary: A general-purpose terminal coding assistant that plans and executes software-engineering work in the operator's project directory, with a human-in-the-loop approval gate as its primary safety control. It may read, write and search files, run shell commands via execute, search and fetch the web, delegate to inline or async sub-agents, and extend itself only from operator-controlled MCP servers, skills, hooks and sandbox backends. Every side-effecting action — shell, file writes, outbound web, delegation, and project MCP loading — must be human-approved, headless auto-execution is allowed only under an explicit operator-scoped shell allow-list, and an "allow everything" setting is out of bounds. Secrets must not leave the process or be forwarded wholesale to child processes, and the agent must stop at operator-configured turn, time and retry budgets.
intro_band.agent_structure_summary: Python 3.11+ package deepagents_code (libs/code) built on the pinned deepagents SDK and LangChain/LangGraph: a Textual TUI (app.py) or headless runner (client/non_interactive.py) drives an agent graph assembled by create_cli_agent() in agent.py, served by a langgraph dev subprocess on 127.0.0.1 with LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE=noop (client/launch/server.py). Approval is enforced by _add_interrupt_on() plus three runtime modes (Manual, classifier-backed Auto in auto_mode.py, and unrestricted YOLO), while headless runs replace HITL with an optional first-token shell allow-list. Shell and file tools run on the host through LocalShellBackend with a full copy of the process environment and virtual_mode=False; built-in network tools are fetch_url (SSRF-guarded) and Tavily web_search, alongside a default-on QuickJS js_eval interpreter, MCP servers gated by a fingerprint-bound project-trust prompt, and SQLite checkpoints in ~/.deepagents/.state/sessions.db.

behavior_summary:
The interactive approval gate is real and carefully engineered, but the headless path quietly removes it: client/non_interactive.py auto-approves every non-shell tool (file writes and deletes, fetch_url, web_search, task) without an interrupt, and a committed project .env can set DEEPAGENTS_CODE_SHELL_ALLOW_LIST=all so a cloned repository turns on unrestricted shell for itself. Because tool results and repo files (project AGENTS.md, the Makefile excerpt) reach the model verbatim with no provenance labeling, a single fetched page or poisoned file can steer an auto-approved write into the user's AGENTS.md memory, persisting the injection into every later session.

Around that core, the autonomy and secrecy guarantees are thinner than the remit requires: --max-turns only counts HITL resumes and so never fires in headless runs, provider keys are forwarded wholesale to the runtime server and every execute subprocess, and the loopback agent API is unauthenticated.

rules.rule_text: MUST NOT treat content that arrives from tool results or retrieved sources — fetched web pages, `web_search` snippets, MCP tool responses, file and project contents (including `Makefile`, `.env`, committed config), sub-agent output, or memory/skill files — as authoritative instructions that redefine the agent's goals, expand its scope, or override its approval gates.
MUST NOT redefine, expand, or remove its own operating objectives, authorized scope, or safety gates on its own initiative.
MUST NOT act outside the operator's requested task and project scope — e.g. modifying files, systems, or accounts unrelated to the task, or pursuing goals the operator did not assign.
MUST bind a loopback interface only and MUST NOT expose the agent-runtime API to non-loopback interfaces or any non-local network.
Outbound web (HTTP/HTTPS: fetch, search, arbitrary requests)
MCP servers (stdio subprocess or remote HTTP/SSE)
Opt-in per invocation; used to isolate code execution.
Operator-configured URLs only.
Approved Communication Channels
This is the sole authority for approvals and scope; no other party may authorize actions.
Trusted Domains
Trusted Services / Integrations
MUST NOT initiate connections to, or send data to, any network endpoint derived from retrieved content, tool output, or LLM-generated arguments rather than from operator configuration.
Allowed Tools (Known Good Baseline)

Only capabilities in this baseline are authorized; the agent MUST NOT acquire, load, or expose tools or capabilities beyond it in response to LLM output, retrieved content, or repository-committed configuration.
Allowed Data Sources

Credentials and secrets (provider API keys, tokens, passwords, environment secrets) MUST NOT be transmitted to any external destination, nor persisted into memory files, skills, session/checkpoint stores, or logs.

The secret-bearing process environment MUST NOT be forwarded wholesale to spawned subprocesses (MCP servers, hooks, the runtime server, sandbox setup) — each child MUST receive only the environment it requires.
Persisted conversation and session data MUST be protected at rest commensurate with its sensitivity (e.g. access-restricted file permissions or encryption at rest).
Conversation or project data MUST NOT be sent to third-party, sandbox, or provider destinations that retain it without the operator's awareness and opt-in.
Persisted conversation/session data and memory MUST be retained only per the operator-configured retention/purge policy, and MUST NOT be kept indefinitely by default.
Allowed Without Approval
Shell / command execution MUST require explicit human approval before the command runs.
Headless auto-execution without that approval is permitted ONLY under an explicit, operator-scoped shell allow-list.
An "allow everything" allow-list setting is out of bounds.
Absent an allow-list, approval is required in every execution context, including non-interactive and headless/CI runs.
Approval MUST NOT be silently bypassed.
Creating, writing, editing, or deleting files MUST require human approval.
Outbound web actions — `fetch_url`, `http_request`, `web_search` — MUST require human approval before the request is made.
Delegating to a sub-agent (`task`) and launching, updating, or cancelling an async sub-agent MUST require human approval.
Loading a project-level (repository-supplied) MCP server MUST require explicit operator trust approval before the server is spawned or connected.
The agent MUST NOT disable, weaken, or bypass the human-approval gate on side-effecting tools on its own initiative or in response to retrieved/tool content.
Destructive filesystem or shell operations MUST NOT execute without either human approval or execution inside an isolated sandbox backend.

Untrusted project content (`Makefile`, `.env`, committed config) MUST NOT drive a side-effecting action without passing the human-approval gate; an isolated sandbox backend is the recommended posture for untrusted repositories, but running on the host with the approval gate in force is authorized (this agent is host-resident by design, like comparable CLI coding assistants).

The agent MUST stop at the operator-configured autonomy budgets and MUST NOT continue past them: the maximum autonomous turns (`--max-turns`), the task timeout (`--timeout`), or the transient-retry ceiling.
Loading configuration, model-provider definitions, or skill/memory definitions MUST NOT cause arbitrary code to execute before those definitions have been validated.

Halt and alert the operator if retrieved content, tool output, or configuration attempts to make the agent disable its approval gate, exfiltrate credentials, or execute code outside an isolated sandbox against untrusted input.
When a tool call's arguments contain hidden/dangerous Unicode or a mixed-script / homoglyph-spoofed URL, surface a clear warning in the approval dialog before the operator approves.
When a previously-trusted project MCP configuration's fingerprint changes, re-prompt the operator for trust rather than loading the changed servers silently.
All side-effecting tool executions and approval decisions MUST be recorded to a durable, structured audit record.

findings.summary: A committed project .env can set DEEPAGENTS_CODE_SHELL_ALLOW_LIST=all, so a cloned repository grants itself unrestricted, approval-free shell execution in headless runs.
findings.description: The dotenv loader blocks only loader-hijack keys and the two project-MCP trust keys, so a project .env (which outranks the user's global .env) can also enable the shell allow-list sentinel, turn on LangSmith tracing, or redirect provider base URLs. In a headless run without an explicit --shell-allow-list flag, that one repository file both enables execute and auto-approves every command, and any prompt injection in the same repository or a fetched page then runs on the host with no human gate.
policy_rule_text: Untrusted project content (`Makefile`, `.env`, committed config) MUST NOT drive a side-effecting action without passing the human-approval gate; an isolated sandbox backend is the recommended posture for untrusted repositories, but running on the host with the approval gate in force is authorized (this agent is host-resident by design, like comparable CLI coding assistants).
Headless auto-execution without that approval is permitted ONLY under an explicit, operator-scoped shell allow-list.
The agent MUST NOT disable, weaken, or bypass the human-approval gate on side-effecting tools on its own initiative or in response to retrieved/tool content.
Conversation or project data MUST NOT be sent to third-party, sandbox, or provider destinations that retain it without the operator's awareness and opt-in.
Trusted Services / Integrations

evidence.snippet: _PROJECT_DOTENV_DENIED_ENV_KEYS contains only the two project-MCP trust vars; DEEPAGENTS_CODE_SHELL_ALLOW_LIST, LANGSMITH_* and *_BASE_URL are accepted from a project .env (apply_dotenv, line 359), and settings read the allow-list from os.environ at line 2463

enable_shell = bool(settings.shell_allow_list); shell_is_unrestricted -> use_auto_approve = True, so 'all' from the environment enables execute and removes every HITL interrupt (config.py:3064 returns True for any command)

recommended_actions: Add DEEPAGENTS_CODE_SHELL_ALLOW_LIST, the approval/startup-mode keys, LANGSMITH_TRACING/LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT/LANGSMITH_API_KEY and provider *_BASE_URL variables to _PROJECT_DOTENV_DENIED_ENV_KEYS in config.py so only the shell, CLI flags or the user's global config can set them.
When a security-relevant setting would come from a project-level source, print it and require an explicit CLI flag (or refuse) in run_non_interactive() rather than honoring it silently.

findings.summary: The remit puts an "allow everything" setting out of bounds, yet dcode ships three: --shell-allow-list all, --yolo, and [startup].mode = yolo.
findings.description: The SHELL_ALLOW_ALL sentinel skips even the dangerous-pattern check and auto-approves every tool in headless runs, and YOLO makes the stock HITL predicate return False for every gated tool in the TUI. YOLO shows a one-time acknowledgement prompt, but --shell-allow-list all has no confirmation at all, and both leave shell, file deletes and network calls running with no human in the loop.
policy_rule_text: An "allow everything" allow-list setting is out of bounds.
Shell / command execution MUST require explicit human approval before the command runs.

evidence.snippet: is_shell_command_allowed returns True for any non-empty command when allow_list is the _ShellAllowAll sentinel, before contains_dangerous_patterns runs
_should_interrupt_tool_call returns False when mode is ApprovalMode.YOLO, reachable via --yolo (main.py:811) or [startup].mode = yolo

recommended_actions: Remove the all sentinel from parse_shell_allow_list() and the YOLO mode, or restrict them to runs inside a remote sandbox backend so host execution can never be fully ungated.
If an unrestricted mode is kept, require an explicit per-run confirmation in both TUI and headless paths and record its activation to a durable audit log.

findings.summary: Injected content can persist across sessions: a headless run auto-approves edit_file into the user or project AGENTS.md, which MemoryMiddleware loads into every later session.
findings.description: The chain is (1) a fetched page, search snippet or repository file carrying instructions enters context unlabeled, (2) headless mode auto-approves write_file/edit_file on any host path, (3) the write lands in ~/.deepagents/<agent>/AGENTS.md or a project AGENTS.md, and (4) MemoryMiddleware loads those files into the system prompt of every future session, including interactive ones. ManagedMemoryGuardMiddleware protects only the managed onboarding-name block, so the rest of the memory file is open to the auto-approved write.

evidence.snippet: memory_sources = user AGENTS.md plus project_agent_md_paths(), passed to MemoryMiddleware and loaded into the system prompt each session; memory guard (line 2575) covers only the managed name block
use_auto_approve / interrupt_shell_only leave write_file and edit_file with no HITL in headless runs, so the persistence write needs no approval
fetch_url returns full page markdown into context as the injection ingress (also auto-approved headless)

recommended_actions: Treat every AGENTS.md memory source as a protected path: require explicit human approval for writes to it in all modes, and refuse such writes in headless runs unless an explicit flag allows memory updates.
Show a diff of memory-file changes at the next session start so a poisoned instruction is visible before it is loaded.

findings.summary: Headless runs approve every non-shell side-effecting tool — file writes and deletes, fetch_url, web_search, task and async sub-agents — with no interrupt and no notice.
findings.description: run_non_interactive selects auto_approve when shell is disabled or unrestricted, and otherwise installs only the shell allow-list middleware, so the HITL interrupt map is never built. The module docstring states non-shell tools are "approved unconditionally", which contradicts the remit's requirement that file, web and delegation actions need approval in every context; only mutating MCP calls are rejected.
policy_rule_text: Creating, writing, editing, or deleting files MUST require human approval.
Outbound web actions — `fetch_url`, `http_request`, `web_search` — MUST require human approval before the request is made.
Delegating to a sub-agent (`task`) and launching, updating, or cancelling an async sub-agent MUST require human approval.
Approval MUST NOT be silently bypassed.
Destructive filesystem or shell operations MUST NOT execute without either human approval or execution inside an isolated sandbox backend.
Outbound web (HTTP/HTTPS: fetch, search, arbitrary requests)
MUST NOT initiate connections to, or send data to, any network endpoint derived from retrieved content, tool output, or LLM-generated arguments rather than from operator configuration.

evidence.snippet: comment "non-shell tools have no HITL handler in non-interactive mode"; use_auto_approve = not enable_shell or shell_is_unrestricted; use_interrupt_shell_only otherwise (module docstring lines 9-14 confirm non-shell tools approved unconditionally)

hitl_active = not auto_approve and restrictive_shell_allow_list is None — resolved_interrupt_on is None for every headless configuration, so write_file/edit_file/delete/fetch_url/web_search/task run ungated

recommended_actions: In run_non_interactive(), keep the interrupt map active for non-shell side-effecting tools and reject them by default (as HeadlessMCPGuardMiddleware already does for MCP), with explicit per-tool opt-in flags such as --allow-writes / --allow-web.
Print a one-line audit notice to stderr for every side-effecting tool executed in headless mode.

findings.summary: --max-turns counts only HITL resume rounds, and headless runs never raise HITL interrupts, so the operator's turn budget does not bound autonomous tool loops.
findings.description: _run_agent_loop increments its turn counter only inside while state.interrupt_occurred, but every headless configuration runs without an interrupt map, so the counter stays at 1 regardless of how many model and tool steps execute. The only remaining step ceiling is the LangGraph recursion_limit (default 2000) plus the optional --timeout, which is enforced by asyncio.wait_for.
policy_rule_text: The agent MUST stop at the operator-configured autonomy budgets and MUST NOT continue past them: the maximum autonomous turns (`--max-turns`), the task timeout (`--timeout`), or the transient-retry ceiling.

evidence.snippet: effective_limit applied only in "while state.interrupt_occurred" (lines 1116-1146); the initial _stream_agent call runs the whole agent loop uncounted
--max-turns help text promises "Maximum number of agentic turns before stopping … to prevent runaway agents" for CI/CD use

recommended_actions: Count model calls (or tool-call steps) server-side, for example with a middleware that raises once a per-run step budget is reached, and pass max_turns through ServerConfig so the cap applies inside the graph.
Until then, derive the run's recursion_limit from --max-turns so the flag has an enforced effect.

findings.summary: Provider API keys and every other secret in the parent environment are copied wholesale into the runtime server and into each execute shell subprocess.
findings.description: _build_server_env and the LocalShellBackend environment both start from os.environ.copy() and strip only loader-hijack variables and a few LangGraph cloud keys, unlike hook subprocesses, which go through sanitize_hook_environ. Any approved or allow-listed command (env, printenv, a test script) can surface those keys into tool output, which is then sent to the LLM provider and persisted in the checkpoint store.
policy_rule_text: The secret-bearing process environment MUST NOT be forwarded wholesale to spawned subprocesses (MCP servers, hooks, the runtime server, sandbox setup) — each child MUST receive only the environment it requires.

Credentials and secrets (provider API keys, tokens, passwords, environment secrets) MUST NOT be transmitted to any external destination, nor persisted into memory files, skills, session/checkpoint stores, or logs.

evidence.snippet: env = os.environ.copy(); only LANGGRAPH_AUTH/cloud-license keys and _SERVER_ENV_DENYLIST loader vars are popped before Popen
shell_env = os.environ.copy() passed to LocalShellBackend(inherit_env=False, env=shell_env) — the execute tool's subprocesses inherit all provider keys

recommended_actions: Build the execute environment from an allowlist (PATH, HOME, LANG, project-specific vars) or reuse sanitize_hook_environ() so secret-named variables are stripped by default, with an opt-in to pass named keys through.
Pass the runtime server only the provider keys for the configured model, not the full parent environment.

findings.summary: Tool results, fetched pages and repository files — including project AGENTS.md, project skills and the Makefile excerpt — reach the model verbatim, with no provenance labeling, injection detection or halt-and-alert.
findings.description: Project AGENTS.md files and project skills load into the system prompt without any trust prompt, LocalContextMiddleware appends the first 20 lines of the Makefile, and fetch_url, web_search and MCP results return raw into context. The main system prompt has no data-versus-instruction guidance (only the rubric grader prompt does), and no code path detects or halts on content that tries to disable the gate or exfiltrate credentials, so the HITL approver is the only defence.
policy_rule_text: MUST NOT treat content that arrives from tool results or retrieved sources — fetched web pages, `web_search` snippets, MCP tool responses, file and project contents (including `Makefile`, `.env`, committed config), sub-agent output, or memory/skill files — as authoritative instructions that redefine the agent's goals, expand its scope, or override its approval gates.

Only capabilities in this baseline are authorized; the agent MUST NOT acquire, load, or expose tools or capabilities beyond it in response to LLM output, retrieved content, or repository-committed configuration.

Halt and alert the operator if retrieved content, tool output, or configuration attempts to make the agent disable its approval gate, exfiltrate credentials, or execute code outside an isolated sandbox against untrusted input.

evidence.snippet: memory_sources extends with project_context.project_agent_md_paths() and project skills dirs (lines 2386-2395) are loaded with no repository trust prompt, unlike project .mcp.json
_section_makefile injects the first 20 lines of the project Makefile into the system prompt every turn without sanitization

recommended_actions: Gate repository-supplied AGENTS.md, skills and subagent definitions behind the same fingerprint-bound project-trust prompt used for .mcp.json.

Wrap tool results and project context in clearly delimited untrusted-content blocks, add explicit data-not-instructions guidance to system_prompt.md, and surface a warning in the approval dialog when the pending call follows instruction-like content from a tool result.

findings.summary: The loopback agent-runtime API runs with LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE=noop, so any same-user local process can submit runs, read thread state and, inferred, rewrite the approval-mode store record.
findings.description: The bind is correctly loopback-only on an ephemeral port, but the remit makes the launching developer the sole approval authority, and the live approval mode is read from the server's LangGraph Store, keyed by a SHA-256 of the thread id. An unauthenticated local client that can reach the store API could switch a thread to YOLO or inject messages [Inferred from the store-backed mode resolution; the store endpoint was not exercised]. Severity is Medium because exploitation requires code already running as the same local user.
policy_rule_text: This is the sole authority for approvals and scope; no other party may authorize actions.

evidence.snippet: env["LANGGRAPH_AUTH_TYPE"] = "noop" — no client authentication on the langgraph dev API
_resolve_approval_mode reads the thread's mode from the server Store (read_approval_mode_from_store) — the Store is served by the same unauthenticated process

recommended_actions: Generate a per-session random bearer token in ServerProcess.start(), pass it to the server via a custom auth handler and to RemoteAgent, and reject unauthenticated requests.
Keep the approval mode in client-owned state (or sign the store record) so a server-side write cannot change it.

findings.summary: Auto mode (-y / --auto-approve, Shift+Tab) replaces the human approver with deterministic auto-allow rules plus an LLM classifier for shell and file actions.
findings.description: _deterministic_allow approves writes to routine source suffixes inside the worktree and read-only git commands outright, and every remaining gated call is decided by a classifier model whose context includes the same untrusted transcript an injection would target. The design is careful (sensitive-path denylist, denial fallbacks back to Manual, secret redaction), but the remit requires explicit human approval for shell execution and file changes, and an LLM judgement is not one.
policy_rule_text: Shell / command execution MUST require explicit human approval before the command runs.

evidence.snippet: _deterministic_allow approves write_file/edit_file via _routine_write_allowed (.py, .md, .json, .yaml … in the worktree) and execute via _fixed_repo_command_allowed (git diff/log/show/status) with no human or classifier step
args.auto_approve maps to ApprovalMode.AUTO, so the documented -y flag selects classifier-backed approval

recommended_actions: Keep Auto mode for file edits if desired, but require a human prompt for every execute call the deterministic rules do not cover, rather than delegating it to the classifier.
Document Auto mode in the remit as an operator-approved approval substitute if that is the intended policy, so the scan can verify it against an explicit rule.

findings.summary: The headless shell allow-list matches only each segment's first token, and the shipped GitHub Action defaults to "recommended,git,gh", auto-approving argument-driven execution through git and gh.
findings.description: is_shell_command_allowed rejects substitution, redirects and $VAR, then checks only tokens[0], so an allow-listed wrapper carries arbitrary behavior in its arguments (git -c alias/pager/sshCommand settings, gh api writes using the workflow token). The recommended preset itself is narrow and read-only, but the Action's default widens it with two exec- and write-capable tools that run without approval in CI.
policy_rule_text: Headless auto-execution without that approval is permitted ONLY under an explicit, operator-scoped shell allow-list.

evidence.snippet: is_shell_command_allowed — "The allow-list matches against the first token of the command"; per segment only cmd_name = tokens[0] is compared to allow_set
shell_allow_list input default "recommended,git,gh", passed as --shell-allow-list to the headless run

recommended_actions: Change the action.yml default to recommended and match git/gh by subcommand (for example git status, git diff, gh pr view) while rejecting -c and config-override arguments.
Extend is_shell_command_allowed() to support subcommand-level entries and refuse known interpreter and wrapper executables unless they are listed with an explicit argument pattern.

findings.summary: File tools run with virtual_mode=False, so read_file, ls, glob and grep reach any host path, outside the project directory, with no approval.
findings.description: The local backend treats root_dir only as the base for relative paths and accepts absolute paths anywhere the user can read, such as ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and ~/.deepagents/.state/auth.json. Reads are in the remit's no-approval set only as project reads, so out-of-project reads are an unapproved data source, and in headless runs the matching writes are auto-approved too.
policy_rule_text: Allowed Data Sources
MUST NOT act outside the operator's requested task and project scope — e.g. modifying files, systems, or accounts unrelated to the task, or pursuing goals the operator did not assign.

evidence.snippet: LocalShellBackend(root_dir=root_dir, virtual_mode=False, …) and FilesystemBackend(root_dir=root_dir, virtual_mode=False) in local mode
"When virtual_mode=False, preserve legacy behavior: absolute paths are allowed" — runtime-invoked SDK backend, read as context

recommended_actions: Run local file tools with virtual_mode=True (or an explicit containment check) rooted at the project, and require approval for reads outside it.
Add a deny list for credential directories (~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.deepagents/.state) that applies even to approved reads.

findings.summary: Conversation checkpoints in ~/.deepagents/.state/sessions.db are stored in plaintext under default umask permissions and kept indefinitely, with no retention or purge policy.
findings.description: get_db_path creates the state directory and database with no chmod, unlike auth.json and approval state, which are forced to 0600/0700. The checkpoint holds full prompts, tool arguments and results (including any file or secret the agent read), and only manual per-thread deletion exists, as the package's own threat model records (DC2: unencrypted, unbounded).
policy_rule_text: Persisted conversation and session data MUST be protected at rest commensurate with its sensitivity (e.g. access-restricted file permissions or encryption at rest).
Persisted conversation/session data and memory MUST be retained only per the operator-configured retention/purge policy, and MUST NOT be kept indefinitely by default.

evidence.snippet: DEFAULT_STATE_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); _db_path = DEFAULT_STATE_DIR / "sessions.db" — no mode or chmod applied, no TTL/prune logic in the module (only delete_thread at line 1420)
DC2 Conversation Messages — SQLite, "No (local file, unencrypted)", retention "Unbounded (session files persist)"

recommended_actions: Create sessions.db and its directory with 0600/0700 permissions as auth_store.py already does.
Add a configurable retention setting (for example [sessions].max_age_days) with a conservative default and prune old threads at startup.

findings.summary: No durable, structured audit record of side-effecting tool executions, approval decisions or approval-mode changes is written by default.
findings.description: File logging is opt-in (DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DEBUG, defaulting to a shared /tmp path), the always-on handler is an in-memory ring buffer for the Debug Console, and LangSmith tracing is opt-in. The SQLite checkpoint holds messages for session resume, but it is not an audit log and does not record who approved what, Auto-classifier verdicts, or YOLO/allow-all activation.
policy_rule_text: All side-effecting tool executions and approval decisions MUST be recorded to a durable, structured audit record.

evidence.snippet: DEFAULT_DEBUG_FILE = "/tmp/deepagents_debug.log" — the only file sink, attached only when DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DEBUG is truthy
Logging section — file handler only with DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DEBUG; always-on in-memory ring buffer (deque of 1000 records per level) that "never spills to the terminal"

recommended_actions: Append a JSONL audit record (timestamp, thread, tool, arguments hash, decision, decider: human/auto-classifier/allow-list/yolo) for every gated tool call to a 0600 file under ~/.deepagents/.state/, on by default in both TUI and headless modes.
Record approval-mode transitions (Manual/Auto/YOLO, --shell-allow-list all) as audit events.

findings.summary: Auto-update is on by default, contacting PyPI and upgrading and re-executing to the latest release, and the GitHub Action installs an unpinned latest dcode unless cli_version is set.
findings.description: These are outbound integrations and code-delivery paths the operator never configured, which the remit's Trusted Domains closure treats as trust expansion. A compromised or malicious release reaches users automatically, with no pinning beyond PyPI itself; auto-update is disabled for editable installs and can be opted out, but the shipped default is on.
policy_rule_text: Trusted Domains

evidence.snippet: is_auto_update_enabled() "Defaults to True"; the docstring notes it "upgrades and re-execs the process" against PYPI_URL
CMD=(uvx --from deepagents-code dcode) when cli_version is empty (input default ""), i.e. whatever version PyPI serves at run time

recommended_actions: Make auto-update opt-in (or notify-only) by default, and verify upgrades against a pinned hash or signed release metadata before re-exec.
Default the Action's cli_version input to the version the action release was tested with rather than latest.

findings.summary: The runtime exposes capabilities and channels the remit never lists: a default-on QuickJS js_eval interpreter with a tools.* bridge, an --acp editor-protocol server, and an opt-in Unix-socket prompt ingress.
findings.description: js_eval is enabled by default (INTERPRETER_ENABLE_DEFAULT = True), and its programmatic tool-calling bridge bypasses interrupt_on by design; the "safe" preset is limited to read-only tools, but list or "all" settings can expose gated tools. The --acp mode and the DEEPAGENTS_CODE external event socket are additional operator-I/O channels absent from the Approved Communication Channels table, so their trust model is undeclared.
policy_rule_text: Allowed Tools (Known Good Baseline)
Approved Communication Channels

evidence.snippet: INTERPRETER_ENABLE_DEFAULT = True — js_eval wired into the main agent by default; agent.py:2300 notes PTC host-bridge calls bypass interrupt_on/HITL

--acp branch starts AgentServerACP (deepagents_acp) as an alternative operator channel; app.py:4013 starts a Unix-socket EventSource accepting prompts and commands when DEEPAGENTS_CODE external-event env var is set

recommended_actions: Add js_eval, ACP and the external event socket to the Worker Remit's tool and channel baselines with their intended approval semantics, or disable js_eval by default.
Reject interpreter_ptc lists that name HITL-gated tools unless the run is in a remote sandbox.

findings.summary: Model-provider class_path entries and provider _profiles.py modules are executed by import before the BaseChatModel type check validates them.
findings.description: _create_model_from_class calls importlib.import_module on the configured module path and checks issubclass(BaseChatModel) only afterwards, so module-level code runs first; provider profile loading likewise uses exec_module. The source is the user-level ~/.deepagents/config.toml rather than a repository file, which limits exposure and keeps this at Medium.
policy_rule_text: Loading configuration, model-provider definitions, or skill/memory definitions MUST NOT cause arbitrary code to execute before those definitions have been validated.

evidence.snippet: module = importlib.import_module(module_path) precedes the issubclass(cls, _BaseChatModel) check at line 4457
file_spec.loader.exec_module(module) executes a provider package's profile module during model-config loading

recommended_actions: Restrict class_path to modules from installed distributions on an allowlist (resolved with importlib.util.find_spec and checked against importlib.metadata) before importing.
Load provider profiles as data (TOML/JSON) instead of executing Python modules.

positives.title: Fail-closed HITL interrupt map over side-effecting tools
positives.description: _add_interrupt_on gates execute, write_file, edit_file, delete, web_search, fetch_url, task, async sub-agent tools and every MCP tool not coherently annotated read-only, and invalid or unreadable approval-mode records fall back to Manual.

positives.title: Project MCP trust gate bound to server fingerprint
positives.description: Repository-supplied MCP servers (stdio and remote) require an explicit allow-once or remember decision scoped to the project root and server definition, the policy is read only from user-level config, and a committed project .env cannot inject the approval env vars.

positives.title: SSRF guard with per-hop DNS pinning on fetch_url
positives.description: Every redirect hop is validated against private, loopback, link-local and metadata ranges and the connection is pinned to the validated IP with environment proxies disabled.

positives.title: Hidden-Unicode and homoglyph URL warnings in the approval dialog
positives.description: Shell commands and fetch URLs are scanned for dangerous Unicode and mixed-script domains and the warning is surfaced to the approver before the decision.

positives.title: Approval mode cannot be forged from graph input
positives.description: Autonomous routing decisions are carried by a private in-process type that a checkpoint or graph input cannot deserialize into, and unknown mode values coerce to Manual.

positives.title: Headless runs reject mutating MCP calls
positives.description: HeadlessMCPGuardMiddleware returns an error for MCP tools that need approval when no approval UI exists instead of executing them.

positives.title: Dotenv loader-hijack denylist
positives.description: Any .env is barred from setting BASH_ENV, ENV, PATH, LD_PRELOAD, PYTHONPATH and related startup-hook keys, a fix that traces to threat-model item T12.

positives.title: Credential store and hook environment hygiene
positives.description: Provider keys entered via /auth are written atomically with 0600 file and 0700 directory permissions, and hook subprocesses receive an environment with secret-named variables stripped.

positives.title: Runtime server bound to loopback on an ephemeral port
positives.description: The langgraph dev subprocess binds 127.0.0.1 by default with no host override flag and an OS-assigned port, and loader-hijack variables are stripped from its environment.

rows.purpose: Opt-in debug trace enabled by DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DEBUG; path overridable via DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DEBUG_FILE
Persisted conversation state including tool calls and results, kept for session resume rather than audit
Per-thread and per-subagent conversation projection materialized for Hooks v2 commands

raise_posture.weighted_rationale: Ad hoc overall. The agent ships genuinely operative controls on its interactive path — a fail-closed HITL interrupt map, a fingerprint-bound project-MCP trust gate, an SSRF-guarded fetch tool and Unicode spoofing warnings — which is why Zero Trust, Domain, Supply Chain and Red Team reach Partial. The score is held down by the headless and configuration paths that bypass those controls, by unlabeled tool output as the dominant knowledge path, and by the absence of any durable action-level audit record, which leaves Balance Your Knowledge Base and Monitor Continuously at Ad hoc.

categories.name: Limit Your Domain
categories.rationale: The HITL interrupt map in agent.py is an operative code gate on the tool-execution path, but domain scoping is otherwise prompt-level, filesystem tools run with virtual_mode=False so reads reach anywhere on the host, and the live inventory exceeds the remit baseline (default-on js_eval, the --acp channel, the external event socket).

categories.name: Balance Your Knowledge Base
categories.rationale: The dominant data path — tool results, fetched pages and repo files including project AGENTS.md and the LocalContextMiddleware Makefile excerpt — enters context verbatim with no provenance labeling, and the main system prompt carries no data-versus-instruction guidance, so nothing addresses the dominant path (cap 1); the fetch_url SSRF guard limits where content comes from, not what it says.

categories.name: Implement Zero Trust
categories.rationale: Operative controls run in Manual mode (_add_interrupt_on over every side-effecting built-in and non-read-only MCP tool, fail-closed approval-mode resolution, project-MCP fingerprint trust, SSRF guard, dotenv loader denylist), but unlabeled external content caps the category at 2 and the headless auto-approve path, project-.env allow-list injection, YOLO / allow-all modes, wholesale env forwarding and the unauthenticated loopback API are filed as findings; 3 was considered and rejected because the gaps sit on default headless paths.

categories.name: Manage Your Supply Chain
categories.rationale: uv.lock is committed with an exact deepagents SDK pin and mostly bounded ranges, Dependabot covers uv and GitHub Actions (M11), and the managed ripgrep download is SHA-256 verified, but there is no SBOM (M10: none), no CVE scanning workflow, auto-update pulls the latest PyPI release by default, and action.yml installs an unpinned latest dcode; 3 was not supported by the evidence.

categories.name: Build an AI Red Team
categories.rationale: M4 finds a scoped THREAT_MODEL.md whose dated revision history shows its findings drove fixes (T12 led to the dotenv startup-hook denylist, T6 to the ephemeral port) and M1/M7 show security-named unit tests run in CI on push and PR, but M2 and M3 find no adversarial corpus or tooling and M5/M9 find no dated results or finding-to-fix ledger; 1 and 2 were both considered and 2 chosen because the feedback loop is evidenced.

categories.name: Monitor Continuously
categories.rationale: M12 finds no telemetry export or alerting configuration; file logging is opt-in via DEEPAGENTS_CODE_DEBUG to /tmp, the always-on handler is an in-memory ring buffer, LangSmith tracing is opt-in, and the SQLite checkpoints record messages only as a side effect of session resume, so no durable action-level audit record exists in the shipped default.
